chapter: Making up numbers, bop and technique
title: Faso's brushes and the wallet on the snare drum
summary: Miller tells how a drummer named Faso played soft with brushes, a quilt and a wallet on the snare, and they compare with loud modern playing.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Trump's kind of blues he used to do, cause of blues. But the band had to play real soft on them you know. We had a boy named Faso, he the first one I see them brushes. And he had a big old quilt like in front of his drum. You know he could raise it up and let it down. When he was soft like that he let it down just cause he liked my foot.
What did Faso hit? Did he just hit the snare or did he hit the other stuff? I mean on the soft numbers?
Well he'd be playing on the bass drum and a pocketbook or something on the snare. He'd turn them off see. Turn them off and leave the pocketbook on the drum.
Yeah that kind of pocketbook. That's a wallet. You can lay it on, they do that now. Just lay a wallet on the drum and make it soft.
You don't hit the wallet you just... No, you hit the drum. That just deadens the sound of that skin. Yeah, that kills the sound.
And it takes the rattle, the snails clean off see.

Yeah, it doesn't rattle at all. Well there's no much call for that. Everybody plays so loud it seems. They blow you out of the place. Every place you go. But would he just hit on the snare? Would he hit the cymbals at all with his brushes or what? Yeah.
Like that. You could just go on the snare. You can start doing that now. Yeah.
Yeah. Well bands must have played pretty different then. They did, Dick. They did. I can't imagine a drummer doing that today. He wouldn't be heard. He'd be completely drowning it out.
What you mean doing it in dances?
No, I mean like on Bourbon Street. Those places.
